params.body:
## Why

Findings (`X-n`), open points (`O-n`) and rules (`R S1-6.24`) are handed out as "the next free number", and pull requests written side by side do not see each other. Last night four of them each appended a finding and main ended up with X-109, X-110 and X-111 each present twice. Git raised no conflict because the rows landed in different places; a person noticed hours later. The same happened once with a rule code. Every collision costs a rebase round and a new PR.

## What

One new file, `tests/Feature/RulesIdentityTest.php`, next to `RulesCoverageTest`. It reads `docs/bedrijfsregels/` directly (no database, no Laravel boot beyond the base `TestCase`) and fails loudly when:

1. a finding number (`| X-<n>` at the start of a row in `90-x-bevindingen.md`, open or resolved table) is taken more than once, naming the line and the "what the rule says" cell of every row that took it;
2. an open-point number (`| O-<n>` in `91-o-open-punten.md`) is taken more than once, same message shape;
3. a rule code is defined more than once as a rule row (`| R <code> |` at the start of a line in the chapter files `1*.md`, `2*.md`, `3*.md`), naming file, line and text of each definition. Only definitions count: the findings file uses the same codes in a different table and is not read for this, and mentions in prose are not rows;
4. any `X-<n>`, `O-<n>`, `R <code>` or `@rule <code>[, <code>]` in a `.md` under `docs/` or a `.php` under `tests/` points at a number that is not defined, naming file and line.

Zero-padded and bare forms (`X-01`, `X-1`) are the same number. The rule-code and `@rule` regexes mirror `bin/rules-coverage`.

Deliberately not asserted: that the numbering has no gaps. Gaps are history (an open point was withdrawn, findings get resolved and moved) and a test that forbids them would force renumbering, which is exactly what breaks cross-references.

## It already bites on main

Checks 1, 2 and 4 pass on today's `main`. Check 3 does not:

```
R S4-4.14 is defined 2 times: docs/bedrijfsregels/14-s4-verkopen-aan-een-klant.md:75 "Een relatie kiezen doet altijd hetzelfde, van waar de bestelbon ook geopend wordt: het ..." | docs/bedrijfsregels/14-s4-verkopen-aan-een-klant.md:80 "De bestelbon- en de offertemodal zijn lange formulieren: de kop (titel en sluiten) blij..."
```

Two merged pull requests (the relation display name in `257b555b`/`12ac92b0` and the modal dropdown in `067fc6bd`) each took S4-4.14. Two findings (X-111, X-113) and two tests (`RelationDisplayNameTest`, `ModalDropdownAnchorTest`) refer to it, so today nobody can tell which rule they mean. This PR touches nothing under `docs/` on purpose (a queue of PRs is appending to those files right now), so CI on this branch stays red on that one test until a follow-up gives the second row its own number (S4-4.15 is free) and moves X-113 and `ModalDropdownAnchorTest` along with it. That is the guard doing its job on its first day.

Made it bite locally as well by duplicating a finding row and an open-point row and adding a dangling reference (not committed):

```
X-2 is used 2 times in 90-x-bevindingen.md: line 13 "De bieding loopt zeven dagen." | line 146 "De bieding loopt acht dagen (dubbel)."
O-3 is used 2 times in 91-o-open-punten.md: line 7 "Tokens aankopen via Mollie." | line 29 "Nog eens tokens aankopen."
docs/bedrijfsregels/91-o-open-punten.md:30 refers to X-999, which is not defined
docs/bedrijfsregels/91-o-open-punten.md:30 refers to R S9-1.1, which is not defined
```

## Proposed next step (not in this PR)

The structural fix is to stop handing out sequence numbers by hand: one file per finding under `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/` and one per open point under `open-punten/`, identified by a slug (`bestelbon-relatie-overnamewagens.md`) rather than a number, with the tables in `90-x-bevindingen.md` and `91-o-open-punten.md` generated by `bin/rules-page` (and `bin/rules-coverage --write`) the way the coverage table already is. A new finding is then a new file, and two PRs adding findings never touch the same line. This has to wait until the current queue of PRs, which all append to the old files, has merged; this test keeps the door shut in the meantime and keeps working after the move (it reads whatever the tables say).
params.title: Duplicate finding and rule numbers now fail CI
